Room.title: Room
Room.description: Represents a chat room where users can send and move messages.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Room entity.

code.description: The 4-letter code required to join the room.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the room was created.

creatorId.description: The UID of the user who created the room.

members.description: A map of user UIDs to their roles (e.g., 'owner', 'member').

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user who can create and join rooms, and send messages.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Represents a message sent within a room.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Message entity.

text.description: The text content of the message.

file.description: An attached file, stored as a URL from Firebase Storage.

type.description: The MIME type of the file.

url.description: The URL of the file in Firebase Storage.

position.description: The coordinates of the message's position on the board.

size.description: The dimensions of the message card.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the message was created.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support a real-time collaborative letter board application. It prioritizes authorization independence and efficient querying. The structure includes collections for `rooms`, `users`, and `messages`. Rooms contain metadata and a code for joining. Messages are stored as subcollections of rooms, and they contain denormalized data (specifically, the members map from the parent room) to allow list operations, ensure authorization independence, and maintain invariants.

Authorization Independence is achieved by denormalizing the `members` map from the `/rooms/{roomId}` document into each `/rooms/{roomId}/messages/{messageId}` document. This eliminates the need for security rules to perform `get()` operations on parent documents to authorize access to subcollections, crucial for atomicity in transactions/batches and simplifies debugging. This enforces that only members of a given room can add/modify/delete messages within that room.

The structure supports the required QAPs by:

*   Segregation: Different data types (rooms, users, messages) are stored in separate collections, enabling specific security rules for each.
*   Membership Model: The `members` map within the room document explicitly defines user roles, facilitating straightforward access control rules.

Each document adheres to a predictable schema, and naming conventions are consistent to improve debuggability.
